Lead bedside learning in a high-acuity clinical environment

Drive excellence, innovation and patient-centred care

Build capability. Lead education. Elevate neurosurgical and trauma nursing practice through expert clinical teaching and innovation.

Employment Type: Permanent Full Time 
Position Classification: Clinical Nurse Educator 
Remuneration: $124,273.70- $128,301.88 Per annum 
Hours Per Week: 38
Located in: Westmead Hospital 

Where you'll be working
Join a high-performing team at Westmead Hospital, a leading tertiary referral centre delivering complex neurosurgical and trauma care. You will work alongside passionate clinicians committed to clinical excellence, research, and continuous improvement in one of NSW's busiest and most advanced health services.

Work within a specialised Neurosurgical - Trauma Close Observation Unit

Collaborate with Nurse Managers, CNCs, and experienced educators

Be part of a culture focused on innovation, learning and patient outcomes

Access a supportive environment that values professional growth

Contribute to a service dedicated to evidence-based, person-centred care

What you'll be doing 
As a Clinical Nurse Educator, you will design, deliver and evaluate impactful education programs that support clinicians to provide safe, high-quality care in a complex acute setting.

Plan and deliver competency-based education aligned with clinical standards and workforce needs

Facilitate engaging bedside teaching and support staff development across all levels

Mentor nurses to build capability, confidence, and clinical excellence

Lead orientation, induction, and ongoing professional development programs

Partner with stakeholders to drive quality improvement and implement best practice initiatives

Ready to make a difference?

Join NSW Health and help shape the future of patient care through education, leadership, and innovation.

Apply now and become part of a team that values collaboration, growth and delivering exceptional health outcomes for our community.

How to Apply 
Apply online by submitting your resume and addressing the criteria listed below by providing examples that demonstrate your ability before the closing date. 

Essential Criteria

Registration:Current authority to practice as a Registered Nurse with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA)
 

Selection Criteria

Demonstrated extensive clinical experience and- or post registration qualification in the relevant speciality and nursing professional development-education.

Demonstrated ability to lead and implement change within the context of best practice clinical care and workplace culture

Demonstrated ability to design, implement and evaluate clinical education at the ward level, and provide support and guidance to ensure an appropriately skilled and qualified nursing and midwifery workforce, working within appropriate models of care.

Demonstrated effective and high level communication skills including negotiation and conflict resolutions skills in addition to proven ability to motivate and engage people in the clinical setting.

Demonstrated commitment to professional development and continuous improvement whilst ensuring currency of practice in the relevant specialty.

Strong commitment to the on-going development-enhancement of nursing practice within a patient centred, multi-disciplinary clinical environment.

Relevant computer skills including database programmes and data entry.

Requisition ID: REQ665111
Applications Close: 5th August 2026

Estimator – Full-Time
Location: Welshpool, Western Australia 6106
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $90,000 – $120,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking an experienced and motivated Estimator to join our growing team on a full-time basis.
About the Role

As an Estimator, you will be responsible for preparing accurate cost estimates, tenders, and quotations for engineering, fabrication, maintenance, shutdown, and industrial projects. You will work closely with project managers, engineers, procurement teams, suppliers, subcontractors, and clients to assess project requirements, develop competitive pricing, and support successful project delivery.

Key Responsibilities
•	Review project drawings, specifications, scopes of work, and tender documentation.
•	Prepare detailed cost estimates, quotations, and tender submissions for projects.
•	Analyse labour, materials, equipment, subcontractor, and project-related costs.
•	Conduct quantity take-offs and prepare cost breakdowns based on project requirements.
•	Obtain and evaluate supplier and subcontractor quotations.
•	Liaise with project managers, engineers, clients, and suppliers to clarify project requirements.
•	Assist with tender preparation, pricing strategies, and commercial submissions.
•	Monitor market conditions, material costs, and industry trends affecting project pricing.
•	Identify potential project risks, cost variations, and opportunities for improvement.
•	Maintain accurate estimating records, databases, and historical cost information.
•	Assist project teams with budget preparation, cost tracking, and variation assessments.
•	Ensure all estimating activities comply with company procedures, quality standards, and client requirements.
•	Support continuous improvement of estimating processes and systems.

Skills and Experience
•	Minimum 1-2 years of full-time experience as an Estimator or in a similar estimating role.
•	Experience within mining, engineering, fabrication, construction, or industrial sectors is highly regarded.
•	Strong understanding of project costing, estimating principles, and tender processes.
•	Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, technical specifications, and scopes of work.
•	Strong analytical and numerical skills with high attention to detail.
•	Ability to prepare accurate cost estimates within required timeframes.
•	Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.
•	Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and estimating/project management software.
•	Ability to work independently and as part of a project team.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $90,000 – $120,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work on major mining, shutdown, engineering, and industrial projects.
•	Ongoing training and career development.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.

Top of the Crop Labour Hire require an Office Manager to join their team in North Queensland.

Position Purpose

The Office Manager is responsible for managing the day-to-day administrative operations of Top of the Crop Labour Hire’s office in Ayr. The position oversees office administration systems, records management, compliance documentation, resource coordination and administrative support functions required for the effective operation of the business.

Working closely with Management, clients, operational teams and employees, the Office Manager ensures administrative processes are efficient, accurate and compliant with company policies, employment obligations and operational requirements.

The role provides supervision and support to administrative staff, coordinates office resources and contributes to continuous improvement initiatives to enhance operational efficiency and service delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Office Management & Operational Coordination:
- Manage the daily operations of the Ayr office and oversee administrative activities.
- Develop, implement and maintain office administration systems, procedures and workflows.
- Maintain accurate business records, employee files and operational documentation.
- Manage office facilities, equipment, vehicles and administrative resources.
- Coordinate purchasing activities, supplier relationships and office service requirements.
- Maintain the company’s information management systems and ensure data accuracy.
- Prepare administrative reports and provide operational updates to management.
- Identify opportunities to improve office processes and administrative efficiency.

Workforce Administration Support:
- Coordinate administrative processes relating to employee onboarding, induction documentation and personnel records.
- Maintain workforce databases, visa records and employment documentation.
- Provide administrative support for timesheet processing, payroll preparation and workforce reporting.
- Liaise with operational teams, clients and employees regarding administrative matters.
- Support accommodation and transport administration arrangements where required.

Leadership & Team Management:
- Provide day-to-day supervision and coordination of Welfare Support Officers who assist with administrative processes, employee documentation and workforce support services.
- Allocate workloads, monitor performance and support staff development.
- Foster a professional, inclusive and collaborative workplace culture.
- Support management with workforce planning, training and succession planning initiatives.

Compliance & Risk Management:
- The role maintains administrative systems and documentation to support compliance with applicable employment, immigration and business requirements, including obligations associated with labour hire operations.
- Maintain workforce records, visa documentation and compliance reporting systems.
- Coordinate audits, inspections and compliance reviews, ensuring documentation is accurate and audit-ready.
- Support workplace health and safety initiatives and promote safe work practices.
- Identify operational risks and implement corrective actions where required.
- Maintain confidentiality and integrity of business and employee information.

Stakeholder Engagement:
- Build and maintain positive relationships with clients, accommodation providers, transport providers, government agencies, medical professionals and community organisations.
- Coordinate workforce support services and assist in resolving employee and operational issues.
- Support accommodation inspections, vehicle inspections and general workforce welfare activities.

Continuous Improvement:
- Review and improve administrative processes to enhance efficiency and service delivery.
- Contribute to organisational planning, workforce management initiatives and business improvement projects.
- Support the achievement of operational, compliance and workforce objectives.

Essential Selection Criteria:
- Demonstrated at least one-year experience in office management, operations management or a similar role.
- Proven experience leading and supervising staff.
- Strong organisational, administrative and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder relationship management skills.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced operational environment.
- High-level proficiency in Microsoft Office and workforce administration systems.
- Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
- Current Australian Driver Licence.

Desirable Criteria:
- Experience working with PALM Scheme participants or culturally diverse workforces.
- Knowledge of labour hire operations, workforce compliance and employment legislation.
- Experience coordinating accommodation, transport and workforce logistics.
- Experience with payroll administration and workforce reporting systems.
- Experience using SharePoint or workforce management platforms.

Key Attributes:
- Strong leadership and people management capability.
- Professional, approachable and accountable.
- Highly organised with excellent attention to detail.
- Strong relationship-building and communication skills.
- Solutions-focused, adaptable and resilient.
- Committed to continuous improvement and operational excellence.

Other Requirements:
- Bachelor’s Degree
- Advanced experience with Microsoft products
- Current Australian Driver Licence.
- National Police Check (or ability to obtain).
- Willingness to work flexible hours to meet operational requirements.

Simmonds Steel is a leading structural steel supplier and fabricator servicing residential, commercial, industrial and mining projects throughout Western Australia. We provide structural steel solutions ranging from small residential applications to large-scale commercial and industrial developments, including design support, 3D modelling, fabrication and installation services.
We are seeking an experienced and motivated Construction Estimator to join our team on a full-time basis.
Position Overview
Responsible for preparing accurate cost estimates and tender submissions for structural steel fabrication and installation projects. The role involves analysing engineering and architectural documentation, calculating material and labour requirements, obtaining supplier and subcontractor pricing, and supporting project delivery through effective cost planning and estimating. Involvement in tender settlement, cost planning, supplier negotiations, and project budget forecasting
Key Duties and Responsibilities
•	Review and interpret structural, architectural and engineering drawings, specifications and tender documentation.
•	Perform detailed quantity take-offs for structural steel components, including beams, columns, lintels, bracing systems, platework and associated materials.
•	Calculate project costs, including materials, fabrication, labour, transport, craneage, installation and subcontractor services.
•	Prepare accurate cost estimates, quotations, budgets and tender submissions for residential, commercial, industrial and mining projects.
•	Liaise with engineers, architects, project managers, clients and contractors to clarify project requirements and specifications.
•	Assess project risks, site conditions and construction methodologies affecting project costs and delivery.
•	Prepare and maintain estimating databases, cost records and pricing schedules.
•	Assist management in tender reviews, contract negotiations and project handovers.
•	Monitor market pricing trends for steel products, fabrication processes and construction services.
•	Support project planning by providing cost forecasts, material schedules and estimating reports.
•	Ensure all estimates comply with relevant Australian Standards, building codes, safety requirements and company procedures.
Skills and Experience
•	Diploma, Advanced Diploma or higher qualification in Building, Construction, Engineering or a related discipline.
•	Minimum 3 years’ relevant experience as a Construction Estimator, Steel Estimator, Building Estimator or similar role.
•	Strong ability to read and interpret structural and engineering drawings.
•	Experience estimating structural steel fabrication and installation projects.
•	Sound knowledge of construction methods, steel products and fabrication processes.
•	Proficiency with estimating software, Microsoft Excel and construction management systems.
•	Ability to manage multiple tenders and meet deadlines.
What We Offer
•	Full-time permanent position.
•	Competitive salary package of $90000.00 per annum plus superannuation
•	Supportive and professional working environment.
•	Career growth within an established structural steel business.
If you have the skills and experience to contribute to our growing team, we encourage you to apply.

Position Overview
We are looking for a skilled Telecommunications Field Engineer to install, maintain and support telecommunications infrastructure across a range of environments. This role is responsible for ensuring reliable network performance, resolving technical issues in the field, and supporting the integration of telecommunications systems with IT infrastructure. The ideal candidate is hands-on, detail-oriented, and experienced in working with complex network and communication technologies.
Key Responsibilities
Install, configure and commission telecommunications equipment including routers, switches, cabling and transmission systems
Integrate telecommunications networks with computer systems, hardware, software and operating environments
Diagnose and resolve faults in network infrastructure, ensuring minimal downtime and service disruption
Monitor network performance and conduct routine maintenance to optimise system reliability and efficiency
Maintain accurate records of equipment, configurations, inventory and service activities
Prepare and update technical documentation, including procedures, policies and compliance standards
Provide technical support and guidance to clients, stakeholders and internal teams
Conduct site inspections, testing and troubleshooting of telecommunications systems in field environments
Ensure compliance with industry standards, safety regulations and organisational quality requirements
Coordinate with vendors, service providers and project teams to support installations and upgrades
Support the deployment of new technologies, upgrades and network expansions
Respond to service requests and incidents within agreed service level timeframes
Required Qualifications & Skills
Bachelor’s degree or Diploma in Telecommunications Engineering, Electronics, IT or a related field
Proven experience in telecommunications field engineering, network installation or technical support roles
Strong knowledge of networking principles (LAN/WAN, TCP/IP, routing and switching)
Experience with telecommunications equipment, cabling standards and transmission technologies
Ability to troubleshoot complex technical issues in field-based environments
Familiarity with operating systems, databases and system integration concepts
Excellent problem-solving, analytical and organisational skills
Strong communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly
Ability to work independently and manage multiple service tasks effectively
Valid driver’s licence and willingness to travel to various job sites
Preferred Qualifications
Industry certifications such as Cisco (CCNA/CCNP), CompTIA Network+ or equivalent
Experience with fibre optics, wireless networks or mobile telecommunications systems
Knowledge of network monitoring tools and diagnostic software
Experience working in large-scale infrastructure or enterprise environments
Understanding of Australian telecommunications standards and compliance requirements
Why Join Us?
Opportunity to work on diverse and large-scale telecommunications projects
Supportive and collaborative team environment
Ongoing training and professional development opportunities
Career progression within a growing organisation
Competitive salary package with additional benefits
Job Details
Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Super
